arxiv-2209-15087.title: Zero-shot visual reasoning through probabilistic analogical mapping
arxiv-2209-15087.creator: Taylor Webb, Shuhao Fu, Trevor Bihl, Keith J. Holyoak, Hongjing Lu
arxiv-2209-15087.description: Abstract Human reasoning is grounded in an ability to identify highly abstract commonalities governing superficially dissimilar visual inputs. Recent efforts to develop algorithms with this capacity have largely focused on approaches that require extensive direct training on visual reasoning tasks, and yield limited generalization to problems with novel content.

arxiv-2302-10701.title: Scalable Infomin Learning
arxiv-2302-10701.creator: Yanzhi Chen, Weihao Sun, Yingzhen Li, Adrian Weller, University of Cambridge, Rutgers University, Imperial College London, Alan Turing Institute
arxiv-2302-10701.description: Abstract The task of infomin learning aims to learn a representation with high utility while being uninformative about a specified target, with the latter achieved by minimising the mutual information between the representation and the target. It has broad applications, ranging from training fair prediction models against protected attributes, to unsupervised learning with disentangled representations.

arxiv-2412-05952.title: A Newton-Like Dynamical System for Nonsmooth and Nonconvex Optimization Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE.
arxiv-2412-05952.creator: Juan Guillermo Garrido, Pedro Pérez-Aros, Emilio Vilches
arxiv-2412-05952.description: Abstract This work investigates a dynamical system functioning as a nonsmooth adaptation of the continuous Newton method, aimed at minimizing the sum of a primal lower-regular and a locally Lipschitz function, both potentially nonsmooth. The classical Newton method’s second-order information is extended by incorporating the graphical derivative of a locally Lipschitz mapping.

arxiv-2501-01193.title: Leibniz’s contested infinitesimals: Further depictions
arxiv-2501-01193.creator: Mikhail G. Katz, Karl Kuhlemann
arxiv-2501-01193.description: Abstract . We contribute to the lively debate in current scholarship on the Leibnizian calculus. In a recent text, Arthur and Rabouin argue that non-Archimedean continua are incompatible with Leibniz’s concepts of number, quantity and magnitude. They allege that Leibniz viewed infinitesimals as contradictory, and claim to deduce such a conclusion from an analysis of the Leibnizian definition of quantity.

arxiv-2504-06391.title: Towards practicable Machine Learning development using AI Engineering Blueprints
arxiv-2504-06391.creator: Nicolas Weeger, Annika Stiehl, Jóakim von Kistowski, Stefan Geißelsöder, Christian Uhl
arxiv-2504-06391.description: Abstract The implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in business applications holds considerable promise for significant improvements. The development of AI systems is becoming increasingly complex, thereby underscoring the growing importance of AI engineering and MLOps techniques. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face considerable challenges when implementing AI in their products or processes.

arxiv-2508-12981.title: Analyzing Information Sharing and Coordination in Multi-Agent Planning
arxiv-2508-12981.creator: Tianyue Ou, Saujas Vaduguru, Daniel Fried
arxiv-2508-12981.description: Abstract Multi-agent systems (MASs) have pushed the boundaries of large language model (LLM) agents in domains such as web research and software engineering. However, long-horizon, multi-constraint planning tasks involve conditioning on detailed information and satisfying complex interdependent constraints, which can pose a challenge for these systems.

arxiv-2511-08355.title: The effect of discrete-time evolution on thermalisation in a lattice
arxiv-2511-08355.creator: Thomas Moorcroft, Alberto Amo, François Copie, Stéphane Randoux, Pierre Suret, Davide Proment
arxiv-2511-08355.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Thomas Moorcroft, Alberto Amo, François Copie, Stéphane Randoux, Pierre Suret, Davide Proment. Particles subject to weak contact interactions in a finite-size lattice tend to thermalise. The Hamiltonian evolution ensures energy conservation and the final temperature is fully determined by the initial conditions. In this work we show that equilibration processes are radically different in lattices subject to discrete-step unitary evolution, which have been implemented in photonic circuits, coin polarisation walkers and time-multiplexed pulses in fibres.

pmc-10523613.title: Experienced career perspectives of nursing students and their supervisors in learning departments: a qualitative study
pmc-10523613.creator: A C P Boskma, F W Wolthuis, P D D M Roelofs, A T van Wijlen, J E van Schie, J M de Man- van Ginkel, E J Finnema
pmc-10523613.description: BackgroundDue to the nursing shortage, positive work environments are needed to retain (student) nurses. More and attractive internships for students need to be ensured. In order to provide more internship places learning departments were developed, which are characterized by a buddy system and supervisors who coaches at least two students during a shift.

pmc-11357446.title: Searching for Novel HDAC6/Hsp90 Dual Inhibitors with Anti-Prostate Cancer Activity: In Silico Screening and In Vitro Evaluation
pmc-11357446.creator: Luca Pinzi, Silvia Belluti, Isabella Piccinini, Carol Imbriano, Giulio Rastelli
pmc-11357446.description: Prostate cancer (PCA) is one of the most prevalent types of male cancers. While current treatments for early-stage PCA are available, their efficacy is limited in advanced PCA, mainly due to drug resistance or low efficacy. In this context, novel valuable therapeutic opportunities may arise from the combined inhibition of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) and heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90).

pmc-11633520.title: OsGRF6‐OsYUCCA1/OsWRKY82 Signaling Cascade Upgrade Grain Yield and Bacterial Blight Resistance in Rice
pmc-11633520.creator: Huanran Yuan, Mingxing Cheng, Fengfeng Fan, Xingfei Zheng, Ruihua Wang, Fengfeng Si, Xiong Luo, Nengwu Li, Shaoqing Li
pmc-11633520.description: As a major crop in the world, the sustainable development of rice is often severely restricted by bacterial blight. Breeding crops with resistance is an efficient way to control bacterial blight. However, enhancing resistance often incurs a fitness penalty, making it challenging to simultaneously increase bacterial blight resistance and yield potential.

pmc-12405155.title: Management of patulous Eustachian tube dysfunction following bariatric surgery: a case report
pmc-12405155.creator: Amr Youssef Arkoubi
pmc-12405155.description: Patulous Eustachian Tube (PET) dysfunction is a rare condition characterized by an abnormally open Eustachian tube, leading to symptoms such as autophony, auditory fullness, and pulsatile tinnitus. This case report describes a 48-year-old female weighing 72.4 kilograms who developed persistent autophony and hearing her own breathing and heartbeat sounds following significant weight loss after sleeve gastrectomy.

pmc-12451301.title: Mapping brain function underlying naturalistic motor observation and imitation using high-density diffuse optical tomography
pmc-12451301.creator: Dalin Yang, Tessa G George, Chloe M Sobolewski, Sophia R McMorrow, Carolina Pacheco, Kelsey T King, Rebecca Rochowiak, Evan Daniels-Day, Sung Min Park, Emma Speh, Ari Segel, Deana Crocetti, Alice D Sperry, Mary Beth Nebel, Bahar Tunçgenç, Rene Vidal, Natasha Marrus, Stewart H Mostofsky, Adam T Eggeb
pmc-12451301.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a condition defined by deficits in social communication, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors, is associated with early impairments in motor imitation that persist through childhood and into adulthood. Alterations in the mirror neuron system (MNS), crucial for interpreting and imitating actions, may underlie these ASD-associated differences in motor imitation.

pmc-12621164.title: CD8 + T Cells Negatively Modulate Ischemia‐Induced Angiogenesis in Mice
pmc-12621164.creator: Xianji Piao, Jin Jingyuan, Longzhu Dai, Longguo Zhao, Yanglong Li, Megumi Narisawa, Shangzhi Shu, Yanna Lei, Xueling Yue, Jinshun Piao, Chengjie Zhu, Lina Hu, Qingsong Cui, Xian Wu Cheng
pmc-12621164.description: Angiogenesis‐related therapeutic approaches to peripheral arterial disease (PAD) deserve attention. CD8+ T cells play important roles in human pathobiology, and we investigated the involvement of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells in angiogenesis in response to ischemic stress. We also examined the mechanism of a component of green tea catechins, epigallocatechin‐3‐gallate (EGCG), which facilitates vascular regeneration in mice.

pmc-12622491.title: Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy in FeRh Thin Films with Coexisting Magnetic Phases
pmc-12622491.creator: Mengting Zou, Yali Xie, Huali Yang, Gengfei Li, Xilai Bao, Yanlong Yin, Wan Li, Wei Li, Chenxu Liu, Huatao Jiang, Mengqi Qian, Ruoan Zou, Baomin Wang, Run‐Wei Li
pmc-12622491.description: The advantages of high integration density, energy efficiency, and enhanced stability make the realization of perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) in single‐layer films a crucial step toward the development of advanced spintronic devices. A theoretical study predicted that the magnetic easy axis of FeRh film would reorient from out‐of‐plane (OP) to in‐plane (IP) directions during the antiferromagnetic‐ferromagnetic (AF‐FM) phase transition.

pmc-13420555.title: From Ophthalmoplegia to Multilevel Atrioventricular Block
pmc-13420555.creator: Anagh Astavans, Andreas S. Barth
pmc-13420555.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Corresponding Author

Kearns-Sayre syndrome (KSS) is often recognized for its debilitating ocular phenotype, but its most consequential and potentially lethal complications lie hidden within the cardiac conduction system. In this issue of JACC: Case Reports, Amaro et al1 describe a 45-year-old male patient who initially presented with worsening ophthalmologic symptoms, including strabismus, diplopia, and external ophthalmoplegia; the diagnosis of KSS was supported by characteristic clinical features and muscle biopsy findings.
